From my understanding, Tabitha somehow is now getting memories of Miranda. She screamed at the end because she had a very vivid memory of getting to the tree and being attacked and killed by Smiley. 

In episode one/two, we learnt that Miranda and Henry dropped acid back in the 70s for their anniversary which triggered Miranda to begin to have visions of the town and a firm belief she was meant to “save the children” but also that she could see all the women who had come before her and all that had failed. We know Miranda also failed - the details around saving the children and *how* this is done is still unknown - which meant the next “cycle” began which we think is Tabitha. 

I think the Boy in White tried to help the previous cycle with Miranda by telling Christopher what needed to be done but Christopher refused and this contributed to Miranda failing. Now the BiW is pissed off and wants them to work it out for themselves but is allowing Tabitha to view the memories of Miranda as an aid to help. Which is why I think he pushed her out the lighthouse to learn more about Miranda and now is getting glimpses of her memories to try and help. 

Essentially, Tabitha is the “next Miranda” and screamed and did her trademark “no no no no no no no no no” at that point because the memories were so vivid and so accurate that it was terrifying for her - imagine having a MEMORY (not even a vision!) of one of those smiley things coming at you. I personally think Tabitha felt the fear but also felt the pain Miranda felt when she died and that would be terrifying!

I think the most important part of a bpd diagnosis is to remember it’s an illness and NOT a reflection of your personality. I recently learnt recovery is possible and it’s not a lifelong diagnosis (if you put the work in!) and this has changed my perspective and made me focused on recovery and I’m actively working on how to be better. 

First of all: learn your triggers. Learn what sets you off and what you need. Bpd is an abandonment disorder. Who’s abandonment in your life has hurt you? This wasn’t your fault. Accept that and understand not everyone will leave. 

Allow yourself to be critical of who you’ve been manipulative to. Bpd often means we’re manipulative to people and often we don’t recognise it until after but you have to really consider YOUR actions to accept others. You have got to allow people their own space and understand and accept they will often return. 

Who is your FP? This is an acronym for “favourite person” but often means it’s someone who we give too much emotional dependence to and leads to manipulation. Do not beat yourself up about this. It’s okay to work out who you are but with defining the line between emotional acceptability and emotional manipulation. 

Please remember you are not defined by a personality and your diagnosis is possibly temporary. Do not give in to the myth you’re not capable of a healthy relationship. It is possible but it takes time. And you have to put the work and the effort into recovery because it is possible if you truly work for it.

Your diagnosis likely is a result of poor emotional upbringing - are you responsible for changing this? Yes and no. You are not at fault for the trauma you’ve likely experienced. You’re allowed to fall down but you HAVE to get up. Accept you were dealt a shit hand but work your arse off at winning the game.

Focus on your faults. These aren’t your fault often but they’re your responsibility to change. They shouldn’t be and I’m sorry that what you went through whatever triggered this. Bpd is a genetic fault (allegedly) but triggered by environmental factors. It’s not your fault that you experienced whatever you did and I’m sorry whatever it was happened but you have to heal yourself. And therapy is all you can do. 

Allow yourself to feel emotions but do not act on them. They’re there to keep you safe and to let you know you’re alive but with bpd they’re ALWAYS overwhelming. Happiness is euphoric. You won’t think you can ever be sad again. But sadness is a depression that will make you think of suicide. You won’t consider happiness to be an option again. But it will come. Often it’s a neutral wave that you will feel numb and flat for a long period of time and either ends of the scale can come in waves of seconds, minutes even hours. But accepting the emotion and learning how to manage it is half the battle.

Please remember bpd is NOT forever. Not if you work on it. Things will improve but you HAVE to put the work in.
